```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day goal is one paying customer. B prices at $29–49/mo per account, aimed at an identifiable professional segment, so one founder doing direct outreach could land a first customer. A earns $3.99/mo per consumer and needs volume, which the brief's own CPI data (~$3.60 per iOS install) makes hard to buy profitably.",
    "B names a cheap, targeted channel into its exact audience: Indie Hackers newsletter sponsorships at about $0.52 CPC across $2,000 spent. A's organic channels come with an explicit note that there is no evidence any of these posts converted to a paid business.",
    "B's pain evidence comes from multiple independent founder posts spanning 2020–2025, which suggests a durable problem. A's demand evidence is one conditional app-store review and one builder's motivation post.",
    "A's case against is severe and well sourced. Artifact had far more resources, collapsed from 100K downloads at launch to ~12K/month by month 8, and shut down. A also faces at least five free or freemium clones and free absorption of the feature into Apple News, Google News, and chatbots.",
    "B has serious problems of its own. Kintsugi, Numeral, and TaxJar offer monitoring for free, and Merchant of Record platforms remove the problem entirely. But B's open questions point to narrower wedges a solo operator could test fast, such as multi-platform aggregation or a decision tool for self-filing versus switching to a Merchant of Record. A's main open question is whether a better niche exists at all."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's willingness-to-pay rests on a single Syft Play Store review: 'Revert the UI back and I'll pay. Until then I'm deleting this and using inoreader.' The offer is conditional, the reviewer was leaving for a different tool, and it is one data point. Relatedly, the case-for claim that Bulletin, KhanList, Content Bite, and Syft are 'already monetizing small niches' cites no revenue or subscriber figures. KhanList is listed with no in-app purchases, and Content Bite's paid price is not public, so that claim counts as unsourced.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-low confidence. Both briefs show free competitors undercutting the core feature. B's brief largely argues against itself: monitoring is free elsewhere, Merchant of Record platforms replace the need, and Tax Threshold Radar may be an unvalidated landing page. B wins mainly because a higher price point, a reachable professional niche, and a cheap targeted channel make a single paying customer within 90 days more plausible than in A's saturated consumer category, where the evidence on unit economics is negative."
}
```
